titleText.es: Leí en un artículo que la ruptura de la simetría electrodébil es la razón por la que tenemos ALMAS. ¡Un tipo con licenciatura lo ha dicho!
titleText.en: I read in this one article that the breaking of electroweak symmetry is the reason we have SOULS. This guy with a degree said so!
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish and English texts are the exact title attributes from the Spanish archive and official xkcd. The unexplained pause marks in the silent opening panel are structural artwork, not printed lexical units. OCR split the visibly wrapped A-/GUA and omitted DEJA; the authored transcript follows the raster.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; makes romper mean that something breaks
cardDefinitions.noteEn: With romper, se presents the named thing as becoming broken, without naming a person who breaks it. The form of romper still changes for the thing and time.

example.es: La taza se rompió al caer.
example.en: The cup broke when it fell.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Vaso names an open drinking container without a handle. It does not necessarily say that the object is made of glass.

example.en: She filled a glass with juice.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; required with convertirse, ‘to become’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Convertir means to turn something into something else. Convertirse uses se when the named thing itself becomes or turns into the result.

example.es: El garaje se convirtió en una oficina.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Convertido is the completed-action form of convertir. After a form of haber and with se, it forms expressions such as se ha convertido en, ‘has become’ or ‘has turned into.’

example.es: El edificio se ha convertido en museo.
example.en: The building has become a museum.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to annoy us; to piss us off (in a vulgar fixed expression)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Tocar normally means to touch or play an instrument, and attached nos marks us as the affected people. In tocarle los cojones a alguien, the whole expression is a very vulgar way to say ‘annoy someone’ or ‘piss someone off.’

example.es: A esos vecinos les encanta tocarnos los cojones.
example.en: Those neighbors love to piss us off.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: balls; testicles (very vulgar; part of an idiom for annoying someone)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Cojones is a very vulgar body-part word. In tocar los cojones, it belongs to a fixed expression meaning to annoy, bother, or provoke someone; avoid it in polite settings.

example.es: La expresión tocar los cojones es muy vulgar.
example.en: The expression tocar los cojones is very vulgar.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: A bosón is a category of subatomic particle. Spanish writes the singular with an accent, bosón, and the plural as bosones.

example.es: La física explicó qué es un bosón.
example.en: The physicist explained what a boson is.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Hablamos is the present form of hablar for nosotros. A time word or a clear sequence can give this present form an immediate future meaning.

example.es: Termina el informe y mañana hablamos.
example.en: Finish the report and we'll talk tomorrow.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that an object breaks, without naming someone who breaks it?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Put se before the matching form of romper.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Use romperse when the focus is the object becoming broken. Se goes before a changed verb form, or attaches to the unchanged dictionary form romperse.

example.es: La rama se rompió con el viento.
example.en: The branch broke in the wind.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: What very vulgar expression means to annoy or provoke someone?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use tocar, a short affected-person pronoun, and los cojones.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The affected-person pronoun changes to me, te, le, nos, os, or les. It goes before a changed verb or attaches to an unchanged dictionary form, as in tocarme. This expression is strongly vulgar; molestar is the neutral alternative.

example.es: Deja de tocarle los cojones y habla con calma.
example.en: Stop pissing him off and speak calmly.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How does the comic connect particle physics with religious miracles?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Water first becomes wine and then blood, echoing Christian miracle and sacramental imagery, while the characters blame personified physics and mention the Higgs boson.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The Higgs field and electroweak symmetry breaking help explain why some elementary particles have mass; they do not turn drinks into wine or blood and do not establish that souls exist. The joke escalates a broken glass into impossible transmutations, then treats the Higgs search as the cause.

applications.explanationEn: Dejad is the affirmative command to more than one informal listener, formed from dejar by replacing final -r with -d.
Dejad is the plural command, de is required, and buscar stays in its unchanged -ar form.
Entonces supplies the later step, so present-form hablamos naturally refers to what the speakers will do then.
